I don't really know yet, I'll figure it out when I get there, in hindsight, I wasn't considering every angle, but I'm not totally set on it — and honestly the whole situation caught me a bit off guard.
Just plan the whole thing, that would be easier for me.
quests.hint: When offered a choice between full planning and total freedom, you can often get the best of both by sharing specific interests while reserving some open time.
quests.explanation: Sharing your specific interests while explicitly reserving free time gets you useful local suggestions without losing the flexibility you want. Asking your friend to plan everything risks losing the unstructured wandering time you specifically valued. Declining input entirely wastes a friend's local knowledge that could genuinely improve your trip.
consequencePreviews: Realistically, you give your friend enough to make genuinely useful suggestions while protecting the flexibility you actually want.
You may notice that declining any input from a friend who knows the city well misses a chance to get genuinely useful, local suggestions.
Realistically, handing over the whole plan may leave no room for the unstructured wandering time you actually wanted.

quests.persona: a boarding gate agent noticing you look confused
quests.scene: You're standing near the gate looking uncertain, and an agent asks: 'Are you in the right place? Where are you headed?'
options: I think so, thinking about it now, I hadn't stopped to think it all the way through, so there might be a better way to handle it.
I'm actually not totally sure — I'm trying to get to the connecting flight to Lisbon.
Airports are so confusing, the signage here is honestly terrible, I've been lost for twenty minutes.
quests.hint: When you're lost or unsure, naming your actual destination gets you the fastest, most useful help.
quests.explanation: Naming your destination lets the agent immediately confirm or correct your location. 'I think so' doesn't give the agent enough information to actually verify anything. Complaining about the signage doesn't tell the agent where you're actually trying to go, which is what they need to help you.
consequencePreviews: The vague answer doesn't give the agent enough to confirm you're actually in the right place.
Here, the agent can point you in exactly the right direction, since you've named your actual destination.
As a result, the complaint doesn't tell the agent where you're actually trying to go, so they can't help you get there.

quests.persona: a hotel guest services line during a mix-up
quests.scene: You call because your room key isn't working and you're locked out, standing in the hallway.
options: My room key isn't working and I'm locked out in the hallway right now — could someone come let me in or reset the key?
There's a problem with my key, I guess, I was just going with my gut on that one, but I'm not totally set on it — and a lot depends on details I haven't really looked into yet.
This hotel's key system never works properly, it happened to me last time too, to be honest, I was going more on instinct than anything.
quests.hint: When you need immediate help, state exactly what's wrong and where you are right now.
quests.explanation: Stating the exact problem and your current situation gets you help as quickly as possible. A vague statement doesn't convey the urgency of being locked out right now. Bringing up a past issue with the hotel doesn't communicate your immediate, current need clearly.
consequencePreviews: As a result, guest services gets exactly what they need to send someone to help you quickly.
You may notice that the vague statement doesn't convey that you're currently locked out and need help right away.
In this moment, the complaint about a past issue doesn't clearly communicate your urgent, current situation.

quests.persona: a rideshare support chat during a dispute over a fare
quests.scene: You're charged significantly more than the estimated fare shown before your ride, and you message support to understand why.
options: This app is a total scam, you're clearly ripping people off, I want my money back right now, to be honest, I hadn't really thought it through, but that could easily change.
I got charged too much.
My fare was $34, but the app estimated $19 before the ride — could you help me understand the difference, and check if this was applied correctly?
quests.hint: When disputing a charge, give the specific numbers involved and ask for an investigation, rather than a vague complaint or an outright accusation.
quests.explanation: Providing the specific numbers gives support agent something concrete to actually check against the ride's details. A vague complaint doesn't give them enough to verify whether an error occurred. Accusing the company of a scam may reduce their willingness to carefully look into a fare discrepancy that could well be a genuine mistake.
consequencePreviews: Realistically, the accusation may make support less inclined to investigate carefully, even if your concern about the fare is legitimate.
You may notice that without the specific numbers, support can't easily verify whether something actually went wrong.
Here, support gets the exact numbers needed to investigate whether an error actually occurred.
